papers.title: Beyond the scan: A critical look at ultrasound for predicting gestational age and whelping in the bitch.
papers.abstract: In canine reproductive management an accurate prediction of the expected date of parturition may influence clinical decision-making, neonatal survival, and the timing of elective Caesarean section. When data of cycle monitoring, as the luteinizing hormone surge or ovulation date, are unavailable, ultrasonographic fetometry is the most reliable method for estimating gestational age. This review critically evaluates the current evidence regarding the use of ultrasonography for pregnancy dating in the bitch, with particular emphasis on the inner chorionic cavity diameter and biparietal diameter, the two most extensively validated biometric parameters. The effect of different factors on the accuracy of ultrasonographic prediction, including operator experience, examination standardization, maternal size, breed, litter size, and gestational stage, are discussed together with the strengths and limitations of currently available mathematical models. The clinical relevance of standardized scanning protocols and to the ongoing debate regarding the value of breed-specific equations compared with models based on maternal size are discussed in depth. The review also examines the fetal maturity assessment during late gestation, highlighting the potential contribution of fetal heart rate, gastrointestinal motility, pulmonary development, and other ultrasonographic markers. Current evidence indicates that no single ultrasonographic parameter is sufficient to accurately predict both the timing of parturition and fetal readiness for extrauterine life. Instead, the integration of standardized ultrasonographic examination, validated biometric models, assessment of fetal organ maturation, endocrine information, and reproductive history provide the most comprehensive approach. papers.title: Improving adhesion and targeting of adherent areas for high-throughput cryo electron tomography of vitreous sections.
papers.abstract: Cellular cryo electron tomography explores tissue and cells in their unstained flash-frozen native state, revealing in situ the structure of macromolecules together with their local environment and interactions with partners, also known as molecular sociology. To obtain thin samples, cryo-FIB milling is nowadays the most popular method, with impressive successes. The alternative, cryo-ultramicrotomy, is often overlooked on account of poorly reproducible attachment of cryo-sections to their support, resulting in low throughput. We optimized the workflow, focusing on section adhesion and their support grids. We thus increased cryo electron tomography of vitreous section throughput, to equal that of thin film, typically leading to several tens to hundreds of cryo-tomograms per ribbon of sections. This opens the way to new advances in cellular cryo electron tomography, as the method is devoid of ion beam damage, and can provide large surfaces and serial sections of any type of sample from cells to tissues, organs or even entire organisms. In addition, section thickness can be tuned down to 30-50 nm, which may be an advantage for imaging small molecular complexes, such as DNA and nucleosomes.

papers.title: Modulation mechanism of L-tryptophan and phosphate to the chicken extracellular calcium-sensing receptor via downstream G protein-coupled signaling cascades and their binding modes.
papers.abstract: Laying hens undergo dynamic bone turnover and have a high demand for calcium due to the daily egg-laying cycle. The chicken extracellular calcium-sensing receptor (cCaSR) plays an important role in calcium homeostasis. This study investigated the modulatory effects and mechanisms of L-tryptophan (L-Trp) and inorganic phosphate (PO₄³⁻) on cCaSR-mediated signaling. A stable Flp-In™-293 cell line expressing cCaSR was established and used in a completely randomized in vitro cell culture design. Individual cell culture wells served as the experimental unit, with at least three technical replicates per experiment and at least three independent experiments. cCaSR activation was evaluated using luciferase reporter assays and a cAMP assay to assess Gαq-, Gβγ/Gαi-, Gα12-, and Gαi-mediated signaling. Dose-response curves were fitted by nonlinear regression, and data were analyzed by one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's or Tukey's multiple-comparison test (P < 0.05). L-Trp enhanced Ca²⁺-mediated cCaSR activation, shifting the Ca²⁺ EC50 by 12.88%, 5.18%, and 1.02% in the Gαq, Gβγ/Gαi, and Gα12 pathways, respectively, whereas the Ca²⁺ IC50 for cAMP shifted by 10.15% in the Gαi pathway. The calcimimetic R568 was used to partially substitute for Ca²⁺ to minimize Ca²⁺-phosphate interactions. In the presence of Ca²⁺ and R568, 2 mM PO₄³⁻ inhibited cCaSR responses in the Gαq, Gβγ/Gαi, and Gα12 pathways by 92.97%, 31.50%, and 30.23%, respectively, compared with 0.9 mM PO₄³⁻ (P < 0.05). At 5 mM PO₄³⁻, cAMP levels increased by 51.20% (P < 0.05). The greatest numerical changes induced by both L-Trp and PO₄³⁻ were observed in the Gαq-mediated NFAT-RE pathway. papers.title: From cultural scripts to financial compliance: Sociotechnical mechanisms and narrative reconstruction in Chinese "pig-butchering" Romance-Investment scam victim accounts.
papers.abstract: Digital romance-investment fraud is often examined through sequential models of scam progression or explanations centered on individual cognitive deficits. However, these approaches offer limited insight into how emotional grooming and financial exploitation become intertwined within the same interactional process. Drawing on 60 retained victim accounts, 16 focal cases, and a broader comment corpus from Zhihu, China, this study combines qualitative coding and latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) to develop the Cues-Capture-Compliance (CCC) framework. The findings identify a structurally coupled process in which multimodal cues and culturally recognizable relational norms, including guanxi, renqing, and mianzi, build familiarity and trust (Cues). These resources are subsequently incorporated into relational frames of reciprocity, shared future planning, and material commitment, through which financial requests acquire relational meaning (Capture). Compliance refers to the financial actions narrated within this evolving relational context, rather than an inevitable consequence of relational capture. Beyond this interactional process, the analysis of platform comments shows that retrospective accounts are subject to competing public interpretations, including support and validation, risk education, critical questioning, and victim-blaming. By integrating multimodal interactional analysis with topic modelling and the examination of public discourse, this study advances a sociotechnical account of how relational trust can be appropriated for financial exploitation and how victims' experiences are subsequently reconstructed and contested in digital spaces. These findings highlight the importance of addressing both deceptive interactional strategies and the social conditions that shape how responsibility for fraud is interpreted.

papers.title: The Separation-Distress Network as a Transdiagnostic Mechanism Linking Relational Adversity, Social Pain, and Psychopathology.
papers.abstract: Relational trauma is a major contributor to the development of mental health disorders. This association likely reflects the social nature of humans and other mammals, whose survival depends on maintaining stable social bonds. When these bonds are threatened or disrupted, individuals experience social pain, a distress response mediated by the mammalian separation-distress network. During early development, this network is sensitive to maintaining proximity with caregivers, as independent survival is not yet possible. Converging evidence from ethology, psychodynamic and attachment theory, and social and affective neuroscience supports the function of this network. Because mammalian brains are inherently tuned to form social bonds, adverse relational experiences can disrupt socioemotional development and increase vulnerability to psychopathology. Neural substrates of separation distress include the anterior cingulate cortex, ventral septum, bed nucleus of the stria terminalis, dorsal preoptic area, dorsomedial thalamus, and periaqueductal gray, with endogenous opioids and glucocorticoids serving as key neurochemical modulators in the separation-distress response. Separation distress and adverse relational experiences also alter physiological systems implicated in psychopathology, including the HPA axis, autonomic nervous system activity, inflammation, and brain structure and connectivity. This paper argues that relational trauma and social pain are mediated by an evolutionarily conserved subcortical separation-distress network shared across predominantly mammalian species. Dysregulation of this network may represent one common mechanism underlying depression, social anxiety, suicidality, substance use disorders, borderline personality disorder, and other psychiatric conditions. Understanding the processes linking adverse relational experiences, separation-distress activation, and social pain may provide insights into the etiology and treatment of diverse disorders.
